question: Who has the highest chance of getting animal bites and stings in rural areas?
explanation: Farmers and field workers spend long hours outdoors where snakes and insects naturally live, which naturally puts them at higher risk. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h1)

question: Why is it super important to identify the exact animal or insect that bit a patient?

options.A: It dictates the required length of hospital admission
options.B: It guides targeted medical management and treatment
options.C: It determines the patient's exact blood pressure
options.D: It removes the need for any tetanus prophylaxis

explanation: Knowing the exact culprit helps the healthcare team give the right antivenom or specific treatment instead of guessing! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h1)

question: Which type of venom attacks the nervous system and can cause paralysis?
explanation: Think 'neuro' for nerves! Neurotoxins target nerve pathways, which can lead to breathing difficulties and muscle weakness. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: A snakebite patient starts bleeding uncontrollably and has abnormal clotting. What kind of venom caused this?
explanation: Think 'hemo' for blood! Hemotoxins mess up the body's clotting system and destroy red blood cells, leading to severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: What is your very first priority when a patient arrives with a severe insect sting?

options.A: Cleaning the wound with warm soapy water
options.B: Injecting local anesthetics into the sting site
options.D: Documenting the patient's exact home address

explanation: Always ABC! Checking Airway, Breathing, and Circulation comes first in any emergency to make sure the patient is stable. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: Thirty minutes after a snakebite, which vital signs need the most careful watching?
explanation: Blood pressure tells you if the patient is going into shock, while respiratory rate warns you of breathing failure or allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: What is the safest way to remove a bee stinger stuck in the skin?

options.A: Scrape it gently off with a flat edge
options.B: Scrub it aggressively with a dry gauze
options.C: Burn it out with a heated needle tip
options.D: Squeeze it firmly using metal tweezers

explanation: Scraping prevents you from squeezing the venom sac attached to the stinger, which would push more venom into the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h4)

question: Why is putting a cold pack on a fresh insect sting helpful?

options.A: It completely neutralizes all insect venom proteins
options.B: It constricts local blood vessels to reduce swelling
options.C: It permanently kills any bacteria on the skin surface
options.D: It accelerates the systemic absorption of the toxin

explanation: Cold makes the local blood vessels narrow (vasoconstriction), which slows down how fast the venom spreads and helps with pain and swelling. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h4)

question: Which of these should you NOT do when giving first aid for a snakebite?

options.A: Immobilizing the bitten limb in a neutral position
options.B: Transporting the patient quickly to a health facility
options.C: Applying a tight tourniquet above the bite
options.D: Keeping the patient as calm and quiet as possible

explanation: Never use a tight tourniquet! It cuts off blood flow completely and can cause the tissue to die (gangrene). [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h5)

question: Why do deep animal bites need thorough washing and flushing (irrigation)?

options.A: To stop deep capillary bleeding inside the muscle
options.B: To cool down the inflamed skin around the wound
options.C: To wash away bacteria and lower infection risks
options.D: To dilute any circulating neurotoxin in the blood

explanation: Animal mouths carry a lot of bacteria. High-pressure washing helps wash those germs away so the wound doesn't get infected or form an abscess. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary medication given immediately for severe allergic shock (anaphylaxis)?
explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving drug for anaphylaxis. It opens up the airways, raises blood pressure, and stops the severe allergic reaction. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: What major risk should nurses watch out for hours after a patient recovers from anaphylaxis?

options.A: A biphasic reaction causing symptoms to return
options.B: Complete loss of long-term memory function
options.C: The development of permanent muscle paralysis

explanation: A biphasic reaction means the severe allergic symptoms can pop back up hours later, even without a new exposure. That's why observation is key! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: What is a common local complication if a snake or animal bite is left untreated?

options.A: Spontaneous regeneration of missing skin layers
options.B: Permanent systemic hypertension in all patients
options.C: Secondary bacterial infection and tissue necrosis
options.D: Rapid increase in red blood cell production

explanation: Animal germs plus harsh venom can cause the surrounding tissue to die (necrosis) and lead to nasty wound infections. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h7)

question: A patient with a dog bite has spreading redness, fever, and pus. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Reassuring the patient that no medical treatment is needed
options.B: Applying a tight tourniquet above the infected area
options.C: Applying ice packs directly to the open purulent wound
options.D: Reporting findings and assisting with wound cultures and antibiotics

explanation: Redness, fever, and pus mean infection! You need to report it quickly so the doctor can order wound swabs and start antibiotics. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h7)

question: Which environmental step helps keep snakes and scorpions away from houses?

options.A: Planting tall ornamental grass directly beside doorways
options.B: Storing household waste in open containers outdoors
options.C: Leaving outdoor lights switched off throughout the night
options.D: Clearing brush, woodpiles, and debris from around the house

explanation: Clearing away bushes and piles of wood takes away the cozy hiding spots where snakes and scorpions love to nest. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)

question: Why is community education on avoiding dangerous traditional first aid practices so important?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any public healthcare facilities
options.B: It prevents self-inflicted tissue damage and speeds up proper care
options.C: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever get bitten
options.D: It replaces the need for keeping antivenom in rural clinics

explanation: Teaching communities not to cut, burn, or rub herbs on bites stops them from causing extra harm and helps them get to the clinic faster. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)
